record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.original_question:
Let V be a cone in R^n, and let H_n(V) be the set of homogeneous
polynomials in n variables that are hyperbolic with
respect to every vector e in V. Describe all linear operators T on
R[z1, ..., zn] such that T maps H_n(V) into H_n(V) ∪
{0}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and let $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a (nonempty) cone. A homogeneous polynomial $p \in \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is said to be (Gårding) hyperbolic with respect to a vector $e \in \mathbb{R}^n$ if $p(e) \neq 0$ and, for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the univariate polynomial $t \mapsto p(x + te)$ has only real roots. Define
$$H_n(V) = \{\, p \in \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n] : p \text{ is homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to every } e \in V \,\}.$$
Describe (classify) all linear operators $T : \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n] \to \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ such that
$$T\bigl(H_n(V)\bigr) \subseteq H_n(V) \cup \{0\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of linear operators preserving multivariate Gårding hyperbolic polynomials with respect to an arbitrary cone V is a longstanding open problem. While the Borcea–Brändén theory characterizes linear preservers of stability/real-rootedness in important special cases (e.g. for the positive orthant or for univariate hyperbolic polynomials, à la Pólya–Schur), no full description is known for general cones V in R^n. Recent literature on Nuij-type sequences and hyperbolicity preservers continues to address only partial aspects.

status_evidence.title: Nuij Sequences for Gårding Hyperbolic Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Following the work of Kurdyka and Paunescu, results were given on hyperbolicity preserving operators on the space of polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses hyperbolicity-preserving operators, indicating the full classification problem remains active and not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Hyperbolicity Cones (Brändén)
status_evidence.snippet: Linear transformations and linear restrictions respect hyperbolicity as long as the direction of hyperbolicity is preserved.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial structural results are known for hyperbolicity-preserving linear operators.
